Subject: Supplier portal enrollment + MSA redline

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement is ready to start the portal enrollment in Ariba, but they've flagged a few gating items that require alignment before we can create the supplier record:

- Signed MSA + Order Form acceptable to our legal team (they attached a supplier questionnaire).
- PO acceptance: our portal currently marks POs as "accepted" after a 5-business-day ACK window unless the supplier returns an explicit rejection. Can Redwood confirm acceptance workflows?
- EDI/PO XML prefix — we will request a feed; need Redwood's EDI test contact and preferred PO schema version.
- Tax / remit information and a completed W-9.
- Certificate of insurance on file (minimum commercial GL limits listed in questionnaire).

I've attached ProcureCo_SupplierQuestionnaire.pdf for your legal review. Can you route the questionnaire plus the draft MSA to your legal team and confirm whether electronic acceptance via Ariba is sufficient? Procurement would prefer to avoid paper signings.

Also looping Tom Jenkins (procurement manager) to keep the portal timeline visible.

Best,
Samantha Perez
Sr. Vendor Enablement, ProcureCo

Date: 2027-04-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Supplier portal enrollment + MSA redline

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed ProcureCo's questionnaire and the items that will commonly cause friction. High level: we can accept electronic acceptance via an approved procurement portal so long as the portal audit trail (timestamped ACK + PO number) is preserved and DocuSign or similar signature is available for the Order Form/MSS where needed. Specifics below.

Key legal notes / suggested redlines (see attached MSA_Redline_v2.docx):
- Order Form acceptance: add an explicit clause that Ariba/ProcureCo portal acknowledgment (a recorded acceptance or automated ACK after 5 business days) constitutes acceptance of the Order Form when accompanied by the platform audit trail.
- Payment terms: ProcureCo's ops team indicated a possible Net-60 request. We should push back to Net-30 standard; if they require Net-60, mark as exception and escalate for finance signoff.
- EDI/Integration: include a short liability carveout for test feeds and a hold-back period during EDI cutover to avoid duplicate shipments.
- Insurance: accept certificates electronically (pdf) but require Redwood be listed as an additional insured only for S3-stored customer data handling; otherwise standard limits suffice.

I've prepared two items attached: MSA_Redline_v2.docx (redlines called out) and OrderForm_Electronic_Template.docx (language that references portal acknowledgment). Please review the redline and confirm whether procurement's 5-business-day auto-accept behavior is acceptable to Ops.

Mateo Alvarez
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
--- attachment: MSA_Redline_v2.docx (docx) ---
